### Metrics and retained findings

[Full process](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/ast-report/process.md), [JSON](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/ast-report/process.json), [review](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/ast-report/review.json), [CRAP](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/ast-report/crap.json), [base](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/ast-report/snapshot-base.json), [head](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/ast-report/snapshot.json), [dispositions](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/validation/metric-dispositions.json). The native disclosure/last-Admin sentence adds no provider operation or boundary; another module for one literal/form layout would add indirection. Neither file is new or drops five points. `members-style.ts` is static CSS with zero functions in complete snapshots; raw MI/CRAP are N/A, with behavior checked in real browsers.

High browser-test MI 11.4269→6.3934: keep all 51 independent JavaScript/width/invitation/removal cases explicit, with protocol mechanics already in drivers. Tests have no production MI goal. Low page-integration Halstead volume estimate has a reason: added public assertions specify disclosure, hidden/visible controls and protected outcomes at one seam; volume is not an observed bug. Inherited UI-02 row/layout findings retain their accepted cohesive-owner/test-matrix reasons in [current parent full evidence](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/555ae4b96b1333ac952416307a41237640a72417/review-evidence/ui-02/614090a1632b27ce40a3d2e38cac9492bac048aa/v1/README.md); no inherited full-stack table is repeated.

All five required changed/new CRAP goals pass with known identities and measured coverage: `membersPage` 3.000140625 at 97.5%; `removalResultPage` 2 at 100%; `sendForm` 2 at 100%; two new callbacks 1 at 100%. Unchanged rows retain “unchanged by this PR.” Base CRAP from head coverage is an estimate. Global unchanged functions retain unknown coverage; required rows are complete. No new history record was generated because actual parent 614 is off main; both inherited main records stay unchanged.

Native `InvitationBrowser::inspectOpenForm` at exactly 10 paths remains in `review.json.nativeReview` as a medium warning under native >=10. The trusted wrapper warns only above 10, so top-level counts omit it without policy change or new suppression. It checks one open-form contract. Current native filesAdded changes 6→8; selected findings, native warning set and trusted policy are identical. Keep the current summary as reported; do not rewrite it to match history.

Global graph still has unresolved `src/interfaces/user-portal/main.ts → ./style.css` on both sides and withholds uncertain edge/cycle deltas. Manual registry/import review supports bounded unchanged ownership, not a complete graph proof.

### Habit-hooks

Exit 1 with 35 retained findings, exactly matching the independently audited historical output; snooze `[]`, no suppression. [Raw output](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/validation/aa8c56bb-habit-hooks.log), [each reason](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/9c02340c6feab59357a30f3550217df911732d0a/review-evidence/ui-03/aa8c56bb7e195e97d2362b2c661cc63a760a5cc9/v1/validation/habit-dispositions.json).

- `test/acceptance/auth/hosted-admin-journey.test.ts:13` (high-complexity): One acceptance journey verifies creation, invitation, fake acceptance, workspace selection, browser/MCP roles and creator-only agreement storage in sequence. Its role/identity assertions need the full temporal story; no production behavior is added by its test complexity.

It prevents offline cases from being presented as live provider proof.

The count and default/inactive exclusions are the subject of the tests.
- `test/acceptance/auth/hosted-workos-administration.test.ts:82`, `test/acceptance/auth/hosted-workos-administration.test.ts:83` (non-essential-comment): Explains why the CSRF token comes from the session answer when an access refusal has no form. This preserves the real protected-form flow.
- `test/acceptance/auth/hosted-workos-administration.test.ts:109`, `test/acceptance/auth/hosted-workos-administration.test.ts:110` (non-essential-comment): Defines which captured provider requests count as administration writes. Sign-in and refresh requests must not create a false mutation result.

- `test/support/container/audit-sender-site.ts:59` (non-essential-comment): Explains why public-shaped addresses are safe in this fixture: Docker prevents overlap and the internal bridge has no Internet route.
- `test/support/container/audit-sender-site.ts:75` (non-essential-comment): Explains why disposable fixture TLS keys have container-readable modes. They are not service credentials.
- `test/support/container/audit-sender-site.ts:182` (non-essential-comment): States the fixture proof boundary: real sender and TLS policy on an isolated Docker bridge, without a live external destination claim.
- `test/support/in-process/browser-transport-site.ts:11` (non-essential-comment): Explains why a real TLS front replaces route interception: Chromium must keep the public hostname and real redirects through the same transport.
- `test/support/in-process/hosted-audit-journey-site.ts:40` (non-essential-comment): Defines the integrated proof: both public channels share real capture while the page operation remains controlled.
- `src/interfaces/web/account/account-pages.ts:13` (non-essential-comment): Records the fixed-text safety invariant. These notices contain no request values, so their fixed paragraphs do not need escaping.
- `src/interfaces/web/account/account-pages.ts:96` (non-essential-comment): Records the write/read separation after removal, including self-removal. A fixed write result must not start a new authorization-dependent read.
- `src/interfaces/web/account/account-pages.ts:118` (non-essential-comment): Explains the recovery destination when an access refusal occurs before the user has an organization.
